correctness.rationale: Use uniform round zero and the correspondence with rooted universal covers truncated at depth t. If p<q, the two cycle directions out of each attachment are indistinguishable to depth p: a branch at distance exactly p appears only as a boundary leaf. The connector direction is also indistinguishable through depth p, even if r<p: after traversing it, the first possible difference in the cycle directions is at distance r+p from the root, where r=k+1>=1. At depth p+1 the two short-cycle directions exhibit two degree-three branch vertices at distance p, whereas the long-cycle directions do not. The connector contribution at that distance is common to both roots (including r=p). Thus the first split is exactly round p+1. In the full rooted cover of an internal vertex, the unordered pair of distances and endpoint types of the first branch lifts in its two directions is an invariant. Distinct attachment types separate the three regions; reflections realize the equal-distance pairs on each cycle, and the unequal endpoint types fix every connector position. With equal cycle lengths the graph can swap attachments and reverse the connector, and the two possible thread lengths are distinguished by the sum of endpoint distances. When all lengths equal m, the cover is the uniform m-subdivision of the trivalent tree; its symmetries identify precisely the corresponding positions of all three threads, giving sizes six and three as stated, and cut-vertex status distinguishes internal connector vertices from internal cycle vertices in the graph itself. This also handles the single-edge connector with no internal vertex. The independent replay (branches/bd292d42-57d2-49ac-abe2-6059f953633c/independent_check.py and full_run.json) checked 13056 parameter triples, including 12240 unequal split times and 16 balanced partitions, against structural orbit labels; the finite replay corroborates and does not replace the proof. Frozen scripts were inspected, not executed.
